body:
Triage: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:devx`, Task, S — lands in `scripts/bump-objectui.sh` (pin toolchain, devx per the lane table). The operator-facing half is what makes this queue-worthy rather than shrug-worthy: the pin-bump procedure is run by hand locally, and on a macOS host the #10495 reachability guards are exactly the code that cannot execute — a maintainer can apply a partially-guarded pin today. Do both remedies from the card: the bash-3.2-compatible read loop for the two `mapfile` sites, plus the loud `BASH_VERSINFO[0] -lt 4` up-front refusal is then unnecessary — if the rewrite removes the last bash-4 dependency, prefer the rewrite alone and prove it by running the self-test under `/bin/bash` 3.2 semantics (or document why the guard is still wanted). Acceptance: `pnpm check:objectui-changeset --self-test` green on a bash-3.2 host (or an equivalent demonstration), unchanged on Linux.

- **Branch:** `claude/issue-12071-bump-objectui-bash3-portability`
- **Worktree:** dedicated per-task worktree off a fetched `origin/main` (Prime Directive #11)
- **Domain:** `domain:devx`
- **Declared file surface:** `scripts/bump-objectui.sh`, and `scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs` only if the self-test needs a new case. Nothing else.
- **Model tier:** opus. Derived: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier scripts/bump-objectui.sh …` → *"no path-derived mandate … the tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call"*.
- **Clause ② (contract review):** no. A local operator script's shell portability. No shipped surface moves.
- **Serial constraints:** none. No open PR claims `scripts/bump-objectui.sh`; last touch on `origin/main` is `e47d5ef61`.

### Scope note — this card is this seat's, and here is why

The title says `objectui`, but the fix lands in **this** repo's `scripts/`. The operative test is the landing repo, not the subject. You may *read* the objectui tree if you need to; you may not change anything in it. If your work starts wanting an edit over there, stop and report — that is a different seat's card.

### Premise, re-verified on `origin/main` at the seat (re-measure in your worktree; do not inherit)

```
$ git show origin/main:scripts/bump-objectui.sh | grep -n 'mapfile'
324:  mapfile -t local_refs < <(
327:  mapfile -t remote_refs < <(
```

**One correction to carry forward:** the card names the gate as `check:objectui-changeset`, and the wiring is

```
"check:objectui-changeset": "node scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs --self-test && node scripts/objectui-range.mjs --self-test"
```

There is no `scripts/check-objectui-changeset.mjs` — I looked for it and it does not exist. The half that shells out to `bump-objectui.sh` is **`objectui-changeset-digest.mjs`** (it copies the script into a fixture tree around line 1513 and invokes it at 1518). That is the file to read to understand how the self-test reaches line 324.

### Zone 1 — rulings, not renegotiable

1. **A fix you cannot demonstrate on Linux is not a fix.** This is the crux of the card and the reason it is opus. CI runs bash 5, where `mapfile` exists, so **the defect is invisible to every PR and so is your repair**. A green CI run proves nothing here in either direction. You must produce evidence that survives that: run the affected path under a shell that actually lacks `mapfile` (a `bash --posix`-style constraint, a container with bash 3.2, or a harness that shadows the builtin), or add a static assertion that the script names no bash-4-only builtin. Say in the PR exactly which one you did and what it would have caught.
2. **⛔ Do not weaken the gate to make it pass.** Deleting the self-test cases that reach line 324, or narrowing them to skip the shell-out, is the forbidden direction — it buys green by removing the instrument. The lane rule is that a gate whose self-description is false is worse than no gate.
3. **The remedy is yours to choose from the card's two, or a third if you can defend it.** But whichever you pick, the operator consequence the card names is the thing being fixed: a maintainer bumping the pin from a Mac currently loses the #10495 branch-reachability warnings *silently*, at line 324, mid-run. A fix that repairs the self-test but leaves the operator path degrading silently has fixed the symptom and not the defect.

### Zone 2 — my assumptions. Falsify them; do not build on them

- I assume remedy (1) and remedy (2) are not exclusive, and that the honest answer may be **both**: the read-loop so the script works, *and* the up-front version refusal so a future bash-4-ism cannot reintroduce this silently. I have not costed either. Measure and decide; if you pick one, say why the other is unnecessary rather than just not mentioning it.
- I assume lines 324 and 327 are the **only** bash-4-isms in the script. **I did not check.** `mapfile` is the one the card found because it is the one that fired; `readarray`, `declare -A`, `${var^^}`/`${var,,}`, and `&>>` are the usual companions. Sweep the whole script before you decide the population is two lines — and sweep the other shell scripts the same self-test reaches, because if this shape is repo-wide, that changes the card's size and I want to hear it before you fix it.
- I assume macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2 is the binding constraint and the card's measurement of it is right. I could not reproduce it — this seat is Linux. That is exactly why the ablation in Zone 1 ruling 1 matters: it is the only way either of us learns whether the fix works.
- I did not read `bump-objectui.sh`. If the source contradicts anything above, **the source wins** — report it and the card gets corrected.

### Zone 3 — suggested route, take it or leave it

Read `objectui-changeset-digest.mjs`'s self-test first to see how it invokes the script, then repair, then re-run `pnpm check:objectui-changeset` and quote its verdict line. The bash-3.2 read-loop the card sketches is idiomatic to the rest of the file, so it is likely the smaller half of the work; the demonstrable-on-Linux evidence is likely the larger half. Budget accordingly.

Report per the os-dev contract. Out-of-scope findings get filed, not fixed.

## PM review — ACCEPT (landing held until CI converges)

Reviewed PR #12142 against the dispatch. Accepted, and two of the things it did were things I got wrong in the brief.

### Zone 1 ruling 1 is satisfied, and by a better instrument than I specified

I ruled that a fix which cannot be demonstrated on Linux is not a fix, and offered "a bash 3.2 container, or a harness that shadows the builtin, **or** a static assertion" — as alternatives. The PR does **both**, and is right that they are not alternatives:

- **Runtime half:** `enable -n mapfile readarray` via `BASH_ENV`, which really does produce `command not found` / status 127 — the identical macOS symptom — and which reproduces the card's measurement byte for byte on Linux against the unrepaired script (`7 failure(s)`, `status=127`).
- **Static half**, because `enable -n` *cannot* simulate parse-level constructs (`${x^^}`, `declare -A`, `&>>`). A builtin can be un-enabled; a syntax error cannot.

That distinction is correct and I had not drawn it.

**R7a is the part I want to single out.** It proves, on a probe script, in both directions, that the harness actually removes the builtin — so a `BASH_ENV` that silently stopped being honoured (posix-mode bash, a future harness change) cannot leave R7b green while proving nothing. That is a positive control on the *instrument*, not on the subject, and it is exactly the discipline that keeps a green run meaningful. The ablation confirms it behaves that way: R7/R7b/R7c go red, **R7a correctly stays green**, because it measures the harness.

### My Zone 2 assumption was wrong, and the PR killed it correctly

I wrote:

> I assume remedy (1) and remedy (2) are not exclusive, and that the honest answer may be **both**: the read-loop so the script works, *and* the up-front version refusal so a future bash-4-ism cannot reintroduce this silently.

That is wrong, and the PR says why: after the rewrite the script **has no bash-4 dependency**, so a `BASH_VERSINFO[0] -lt 4` refusal would refuse on precisely the host it now supports — a macOS operator told to go install another bash to run a script that already works on theirs. Not redundant: *actively wrong*.

And the real concern behind my suggestion — a future bash-4-ism creeping back — is better served by the static scan, which strictly dominates a runtime guard on it: the scan fires at authoring time, on Linux, on every PR touching the file, whereas a version check fires only on a Mac and only once someone runs the script by hand. A bash-4-ism inside a script gated on `BASH_VERSINFO` is still a bash-4-ism.

Recorded as a PM error. The Zone 2 mechanism did its job — that assumption was flagged as mine to falsify, and it was falsified with a reason rather than quietly worked around.

### The card's own characterization was corrected, in the sharper direction

The card (and my brief, following it) called this a silent degradation. Measured, it is not: `set -e` kills the run at 127 **before the first mutation of the working tree**, so the operator is not handed a half-applied pin. What they get is a bare `mapfile: command not found` standing exactly where a nine-line warning about an unpushed pin should have been, and a bump that did nothing.

The PR then names the consequence that actually matters, which neither the card nor I had reasoned to: the obvious next move — hand-edit `.objectui-sha`, since "the script is broken" — **walks around every guard in the file, including the one that was trying to speak.** That is a worse failure than silent degradation, and it is the argument for the card, not against it.

### The sweep answered my Zone 2 question, and the answer is "no"

I asked whether the population is really two lines before treating it as two lines. Answer: **yes in this file** (all 17 tracked `*.sh` swept for the full construct set), **no in the repo** — three more scripts, filed as **#12141**.

⚠️ **And one of the three matters more than its line count.** `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh:585` uses `readarray`, and `pnpm sdui:manifest` is *the next step of this very procedure* — the step `bump-objectui.sh` itself prints as `→ NEXT STEP` on the way out, and one with no CI path by decision (#5960).

So I will not overstate what this PR achieves. **This card is done; the operator journey is not.** A maintainer bumping the pin from a Mac now gets past the bump and stops one command later, at the step the fixed script just told them to run. That is the honest status, and #12141 is where the rest of it lives. Filing rather than widening was the correct call — `gen-sdui-manifest.sh` is outside the declared file surface and my brief said out-of-scope findings get filed — but "correct scope" and "problem solved" are different claims and only the first one holds today.

⛔ #12141 carries **no labels at all**. Grading it is the triage seat's, not this seat's — I am not labelling it. Flagging it here so it does not sit unswept: it is a bare-root card and its sharp instance sits inside a documented hand-run procedure.

### Also checked

- No existing case deleted, narrowed, or skipped — R1–R6 untouched and still driving the shell-out. That was Zone 1 ruling 2 and it holds.
- Ablation restore verified byte-identical against a pre-ablation snapshot (`diff` empty), `trap … EXIT INT TERM` throughout.
- The two load-bearing shell details are commented in place, and both are real: `if [[ -n … ]]` rather than a trailing `&&`-list (under `set -euo pipefail` a false `&&` as the loop body's last command makes the whole `while` return 1 — and the empty-ref-list case is exactly the "never pushed" branch this warning exists for), and `local ref_line=''` rather than bare `local` under `set -u`. Both are the kind of thing that would have turned into a fresh bug.
- The ablation output's line number (`346`) is post-fix numbering, not a contradiction of the card's `324`/`327` — the file grew by the read loops and comments. Checked rather than assumed.

### Landing condition

Held. CI started 11:11Z; at review time **zero failures**, with `Lint & Repo Gates`, all six `Test Core` shards, the four `Type Check` jobs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Check Changeset` still `in_progress`. Per standing rule: `in_progress` is not a pass and the aggregate status is not a substitute for the named gate jobs. Flip-ready only when every one reports `completed` + `success` — and `check:objectui-changeset` is the one that carries this fix's own instrument, so it is the one that matters most here.
